proposed_identity.title: Universal state hub I: SAN engine and the thin Lichess PGN reader

operations.body:
# Intent

Stand up the first half of the universal notation layer so corpus building can
start without waiting for the full PGN parser: a hand-written SAN engine over
the canonical `GameState`, a `knightlm-notation` crate skeleton with a
format-detection seam, and a thin streaming reader for Lichess bulk-DB PGN
that turns zst month files into provenance-carrying `GameRecord`s.

## Out of scope

- Full PGN fidelity: comments, NAGs, recursive variations — KLM-WAR-0003.
- Other notations (X-FEN, Shredder-FEN, EPD, UCI move lists, long algebraic,
  ICCF, descriptive) and first-class FRC ingest — KLM-WAR-0004.
- Labeling, joins, splits, engines — KLM-WAR-0005 and KLM-WAR-0007.

# Basis

## Sources

- KnightLM SAS revision 0.2.1 (sha256 f634dbd65e4a, proposed): §98 Phase 2 —
  Universal state hub; KLM-SAS-RQ-004 and KLM-SAS-RQ-006 (§106).
- `code/README.md` "upstream warts": Lichess bulk export emits four-field FENs
  and `UCI_Chess960` PV keys; heterogeneous analysis depths exist in the eval
  side, not the game side. A four-field-FEN source never yields
  `history_complete: true` (KLM-SAS-RQ-006).
- cozy-chess 0.3.4 provides move generation but has no SAN parser or writer
  (checked against docs.rs). The SAN engine is hand-written here.
- Lichess database facts (database.lichess.org, fetched from the live site on
  2026-10): bulk game export is monthly `.pgn.zst`; the thin reader only needs
  the Seven-Tag Roster plus movetext.

## Prerequisites

- `code/crates/core` compiles and `cargo test -p knightlm-core` passes today.

## Open questions

None: scope boundaries were settled with the sponsor on 2026-10-20.

# Work Order

## Deliverables

1. New crate `code/crates/notation/` (`knightlm-notation`) with:
   - a SAN writer and parser over `knightlm_core::GameState`: piece moves,
     captures, disambiguation (file and rank letters), promotions including
     under-promotions, castling, check and mate suffixes;
   - a format-detection seam with `Format::{San, Pgn}` today (variants are
     added by KLM-WAR-0003/0004 additively);
   - a thin Lichess bulk-DB reader: zstd-decompressed month PGN to an iterator
     of `GameRecord`s, carrying `source` provenance (`lichess-bulk/<YYYY-MM>`)
     and `history_complete` per KLM-SAS-RQ-006.
2. `knightlm-notation` CLI additions: `ingest --input <file.pgn.zst> --out
   <dir>` writing shard JSONL plus a manifest row per run.
3. A fixture corpus under `code/crates/notation/tests/`: hand-authored SAN
   edge cases plus real excerpts of Lichess month files (excerpted from a
   file a team member downloads; nothing auto-downloads).

## Seams and who depends on them

1. **SEAM `nota-reader`** — `knightlm_notation::reader::open(path) -> impl
   Iterator<Item = GameRecord>`. Contract: yields records or fails with an
   error carrying position and token; never silently drops or repairs a game.
   Consumers: KLM-WAR-0007 (corpus ingest) and KLM-WAR-0003 (shares the
   fixture corpus).
2. **SEAM `nota-detect`** — `knightlm_notation::detect(&[u8]) -> Format`.
   Consumers: KLM-WAR-0004 (adds variants), KLM-WAR-0010 (viewer ingest).
3. Frozen without change in this Warrant: the `knightlm-core` public API and
   the `GameRecord`/`GameState` schemas, provenance fields included.

## Owner's space

Inside the two seams the performer owns the rest: parser representations and
error types, streaming and buffering strategy, test layout and fixture
choice, CLI ergonomics, internal module structure. Improving the interior so
downstream consumers get a better tool is in scope; changing a seam is not —
a seam change is an amendment negotiated with the named consumers.

## Premade instructions

- `cargo test -p knightlm-notation` after every interior change.
- Never silently repair: a malformed game is an explicit error (RQ-004).

## Autonomy and escalation

Tier T2: the performer builds, tests and reports; the human authorizes and
resolves. A seam change request escalates to the sponsor.

## Rollback

Remove `code/crates/notation/` and the CLI command; nothing outside the crate
depends on the new seams yet.

# Assurance

## Acceptance Obligations

### OBL-001 — SAN writer and parser round-trip the fixture battery
- **scope:** every SAN fixture in `code/crates/notation/tests/`: disambiguation, captures,
promotions including under-promotions, castling, check and mate suffixes
- **evidence:** `cargo test -p knightlm-notation` round-trip tests green on the whole battery
### OBL-002 — the parser refuses a SAN that names no legal move
- **scope:** the same fixture battery, planted with illegal and ambiguous SAN tokens
- **evidence:** planted token exercises produce the specific refusal error naming position and
token; no fallback guess, no silent repair (KLM-SAS-RQ-004)
### OBL-003 — the thin reader yields provenance-carrying records or explicit failure
- **scope:** one real Lichess month-file excerpt ingested end to end; a planted malformed movetext game
- **evidence:** records carry source `lichess-bulk/<month>` and policy-correct
`history_complete`; the planted game produces a position-and-token error
### OBL-004 — the consumer ingests without the author
- **scope:** KLM-WAR-0007's ingest stage run by MLOps, not by this Warrant's author
- **gate:** gate://software.repo.war-check@1.0.0
- **evidence:** recorded cross-lane consumer check: month file to shard JSONL + manifest via
the CLI, unaided

## Gate Adequacy

Required at `basic`.

**Adversarial question:** Can this Warrant be satisfied while a four-field-FEN source is marked `history_complete: true`?

- **outcome:** no — OBL-003 states the policy and the reader tests include such a source.

**Adversarial question:** Can the corpus start even though this Warrant's reader skips annotations?

- **outcome:** no counterexample — the thin reader is exactly the path that allows it; fidelity belongs to KLM-WAR-0003.


## Residual Risk

Real-world Lichess movetext may deviate from spec in ways the thin reader
must refuse rather than repair; the refusal rate on a real excerpt is the
signal to watch. Zst streaming memory is bounded but a hostile month file
could stress it; fixtures include one large excerpt.

durable_choices.statement: Hand-written SAN over cozy-chess 0.3.4; no second movegen dependency.
rationale: The repo standardizes on cozy-chess; a second movegen engine is a seam the team rejected on 2026-10-20.
durable_choices.proposed_adr_draft:
# ADR: SAN is hand-written over cozy-chess

## Context

cozy-chess 0.3.4 provides move generation without SAN. Phase 2 needs a SAN
engine over the canonical GameState. A second movegen dependency would fork
canonical state semantics between crates.

## Decision

`knightlm-notation` implements SAN read and write directly over
`knightlm_core::GameState`. No shakmaty, no ported python-chess logic.

## Consequences

Roughly 500 lines of owned parser code with a property and refusal battery.
SAN stays in lockstep with the canonical compiler by construction.

durable_choices.statement: The thin reader is a separate fast path from W-0003's full parser; both share the notation seams.
alternatives: build the corpus from non-PGN exports
rationale: Corpus urgency is a Phase 5 gate; full PGN fidelity must not hold it hostage.
durable_choices.proposed_adr_draft:
# ADR: two PGN paths, one seam line

## Context

Phase 5 (data pipeline) cannot start until bulk Lichess games ingest. Full
PGN fidelity is Phase 2 work that must not gate it.

## Decision

The thin reader (KLM-WAR-0002) consumes the Seven-Tag Roster plus movetext
only; the full parser (KLM-WAR-0003) is a separate module sharing the
nota seams. Neither silently repairs the other.

## Consequences

Corpus work starts weeks earlier; the cost is PGN features absent from the
thin path by design, proven explicitly by fixtures.

risk_assessment:
Real-world Lichess movetext may deviate from spec in ways the thin reader
must refuse rather than repair; the refusal rate on a real excerpt is the
signal to watch. Zst streaming memory is bounded but a hostile month file
could stress it; fixtures include one large excerpt.
adequacy_attacks: Can this Warrant be resolved without any real Lichess data ever flowing through the reader? The reader obligation cites a real month-file excerpt, so no.
Could the thin reader silently mark games complete when the tags are absent? OBL-003 pins history_complete policy and includes that case.
